Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery so everyone is aligned: 

Summary of needs:
- Primary workload: short classification + context-enriched responses from customer logs (multilingual).
- Target throughput: ~50 TPS sustained for 95% of windows, occasional spikes to 150 TPS for short bursts.
- Latency target: p95 <= 300ms end-to-end for single-turn requests.
- Quality constraints: minimal classification regression vs current on-prem model; we’ll validate with your 1k labeled prompt set.
- Security/ops: VPC private deployment preferred for PoC; audit logs and encryption required.

Recommended initial plan:
1) PoC with two model variants so we can trade cost vs quality:
   - Llama-3-70B (q4f16) — chosen for headroom and better few-shot reasoning; expected to give best quality for edge cases.
   - Llama-3-13B (int8/quantized) — lower-cost baseline for throughput tests and real-time traffic.
2) Run Redwood-verified benchmarks (attached spreadsheet) using a prompt set derived from your labeled data + our standard evals.
3) Compare quality with your baseline using the attached prompt set (prompt_sets_acme_v1.jsonl).
4) If quality and latency look good, scope a 6-week PoC: benchmark, integration, verification, and SLO definition.

I attached the benchmark workbook and the prompt set we discussed. Also dropping the public benchmark folder and the Redwood profile links below. The attached workbook includes per-model TPS curves, latency percentiles, and the raw run IDs.

Next steps (action items):
- Samantha/Tom: review the attached prompt set and let us know any additional test cases by Fri 2/27.
- Alex/Marissa: prepare Redwood-verified perf profiles for the two model variants and confirm instance sizing.
- All: schedule a 30-min follow-up on Wed 3/4 at 10:00 AM PST to review results and finalize PoC scope (I’ll send a calendar invite).

Attachments: model_benchmark_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), prompt_sets_acme_v1.jsonl (jsonl prompt set)

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,

Hey Samantha — nice to meet you (virtually). Sharing a concise Redwood-verified performance profile for the two variants below. Full run results and raw logs are in the attached workbook and the Drive folder.

Redwood-verified profiles (short):

1) Llama-3-70B (q4f16) — recommended for quality-focused PoC
   - Instance shape: 8xA100-80GB equivalent (dedicated or private pool)
   - Steady-state throughput (single model, optimized runtime/batching): 45-60 TPS (depends on batch/sequence length)
   - Latency (end-to-end, avg over production-like traffic using your prompt-length distribution): p50 ~ 60-90 ms, p90 ~ 180-240 ms, p95 ~ 270-320 ms
   - Cold-start: one-off start-ups add ~100-300 ms depending on KV warmness; we bake in prefix caching for repeated contexts.
   - Quality note: quantized q4f16 shows negligible classification delta (<1.5% absolute) on our labelled evals for similar workloads. We recommend running your labeled set to verify exact delta.

2) Llama-3-13B (int8/q4f16) — recommended for cost-conscious baseline
   - Instance shape: 4xA10/A30-class or equivalent in Redwood Dedicated
   - Steady-state throughput: 120-200 TPS (with continuous batching and async RPCs)
   - Latency: p50 ~ 25-50 ms, p90 ~ 80-140 ms, p95 ~ 150-220 ms
   - Cold-start: ~80-200 ms extra depending on warm cache
   - Quality note: int8 quant yields a moderate delta in edge-case classification (~2-4%); often acceptable for high-throughput flows but verify on your labeled set.

Test harness & methodology:
- Load shape: mixture of Poisson-arrival single-turn requests and replay-of-production traces for 30-60 minute windows to capture tail behavior.
- Concurrency: tuned per instance type; Cedar runtime uses continuous batching with latency SLOs enforced per-route.
- KV/long-context: we use KV cache warm-up and prefix caching for repeated contexts; long-context (8k) increases memory and can reduce TPS by ~20-30% depending on token distribution — we recommend measuring the PoC on representative traces.
- Artifacts: run IDs and raw perf logs are in the spreadsheet (sheet: raw_runs) and the Drive folder.

Links & artifacts:
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_link
- Public benchmark page: https://redwood-inference.com/benchmarks/acme-2026
- HubSpot deal record: HubSpot:112233

If you want, we can also deliver a short delta-eval report that runs your 1k labeled prompts against the two variants and highlights any quality regressions by label class. That’s typically a 3-5 day turnaround once we have the set.
